title: Sort Integers by Set Bits
description: Given an integer array `arr` of non-negative integers, sort the integers in ascending order by the number of `1`s in their binary representation. If two or more integers have the same number of set bits, sort them in ascending order of their numeric value. Return the sorted array.
hints: Use a composite sort key `(popcount(x), x)` for each element.
Since `x <= 10^5 < 2^17`, you can even pack `(popcount(x) << 20) | x` into a single 32-bit integer to sort primitives in-place.

examples.explanation: 0 has 0 set bits; [1,2,4,8] have 1 set bit; [3,5,6] have 2 set bits; 7 has 3 set bits.
Every power of two has exactly 1 set bit, so ties are broken in ascending numeric order.
0 has 0 set bits, 1 has 1, 3 has 2, and 7 has 3.
